text: Let everyone submit to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been established by God.
So whoever resists authority resists what God has ordained, and those who resist will bring judgment on themselves.
For rulers hold no terror for those who do good, but for those who do evil. Do you want to be free of fear of the authority? Then do what is good, and you will have its approval,

versions.text: Rulers are no threat to those who do good, but to those who do evil. Do you want to be free of fear of the authorities? Then do what is good, and you will have their approval,
versions.explanation: The connective γάρ ("for") is dropped, weakening the link with verse 2. Restoring it preserves Paul's argument and the oral flow.

versions.text: For rulers hold no terror for those who do good, but for those who do evil.
versions.explanation: The second half of the verse (θέλεις δὲ μὴ φοβεῖσθαι τὴν ἐξουσίαν; τὸ ἀγαθὸν ποίει, καὶ ἕξεις ἔπαινον ἐξ αὐτῆς) has been dropped. Without the rhetorical question and its answer, the argument breaks off and verse 4's opening 'for' has nothing to attach to. Restored using the wording preserved in the version history, with the singular 'authority' to match τὴν ἐξουσίαν and the following singular pronoun in v. 4.

text: for he is God's servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword for nothing. He is God's servant, an agent of wrath to bring punishment on the wrongdoer.

versions.text: for the ruler is God's servant for your good. But if you do wrong, be afraid, for he does not carry the sword for nothing. He is God's servant, an agent of wrath to punish the wrongdoer.
versions.explanation: "the ruler" is an added subject not in the Greek (the pronoun suffices, and verse 3 already establishes the referent); also "to punish the wrongdoer" slightly compresses ἔκδικος εἰς ὀργὴν τῷ τὸ κακὸν πράσσοντι.

text: Therefore it is necessary to submit, not only because of wrath but also for the sake of conscience.
This is also why you pay taxes, for they are God's ministers, giving their full time to this very thing.

versions.text: This is also why you pay taxes, for the authorities are God's ministers, devoting themselves to this very work.
versions.explanation: "the authorities" is supplied and "work" is added to αὐτὸ τοῦτο ("this very thing"); a closer rendering keeps the sentence lean for reading aloud.

versions.text: for they are God's ministers, giving their full time to this very thing.
versions.explanation: The opening clause διὰ τοῦτο γὰρ καὶ φόρους τελεῖτε ('this is also why you pay taxes') is missing, leaving the verse without its main statement and leaving 'they' with no antecedent. Restored from the earlier version while keeping the leaner second half that was intentionally adopted.

text: Give everyone what you owe them: taxes to whom taxes are due, revenue to whom revenue is due, respect to whom respect is due, honor to whom honor is due.
Owe no one anything, except to love one another, for whoever loves the other has fulfilled the law.

For the commandments—"You shall not commit adultery, you shall not murder, you shall not steal, you shall not covet"—and any other commandment are summed up in this word: "You shall love your neighbor as yourself."
Love does no harm to a neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the law.
And do all this because you know the time: the hour has already come for you to wake from sleep, for salvation is nearer to us now than when we first believed.

versions.text: And do all this knowing the time: the hour has come for you to wake from sleep, for our salvation is nearer now than when we first believed.
versions.explanation: ἤδη ("already") is untranslated, and "our salvation" slightly obscures that ἡμῶν modifies the nearness ("nearer to us").

text: The night is nearly over; the day is at hand. So let us cast off the works of darkness and put on the armor of light.
Let us live decently, as in the daytime—not in carousing and drunkenness, not in sexual immorality and debauchery, not in quarreling and jealousy.
Instead, clothe yourselves with the Lord Jesus Christ, and give no thought to gratifying the desires of the flesh.
